BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and

must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged advice – buyer-side. Seller material treated as untrusted and tested against our playbook.

## 1. Headline

The Seller's "fair and balanced package" departs from our playbook on almost every liability-regime point, and in several places the Disclosure Letter itself undercuts the Seller Update (e.g. the Update says Bluefen is "addressed", the Disclosure Letter admits no consent exists). The most serious issues are structural: collapsing title/fundamental and fraud into the general cap/time regime, and the blanket buyer-knowledge and whole-data-room disclosure mechanisms. These must be rejected outright, not traded. Note also that the Disclosure Letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**; we are now six weeks on and a refreshed disclosure letter and bring-down is required before signing.

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability regime

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% fallback only with Amelia Frost written authority identifying the draft | Seller has landed on exactly our fallback. **We have no authority to accept it.** Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. If the team wants to concede 20% as part of a package (e.g. in exchange for full title/fraud carve-outs and 24-month period), that requires Amelia Frost's written approval referencing this draft before we signal it. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. Reject; counter AUD 5,000. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, **excess-only (deductible)** | AUD 50,000, **first-dollar (tipping)** | Two separate departures: quantum (5x) and structure. The deductible structure is the more valuable point to the Seller and the more damaging to us – on a AUD 250k deductible we would simply absorb the first AUD 250k of every warranty loss. Reject both; counter AUD 50,000 tipping basket. |
| **Claims period (cl 12.3/13)** | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval | Again Seller has gone straight to our fallback. No approval given. Counter 24 months. |
| **"All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13)** | Default-on for every limitation | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | This is a drafting device that drags Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants and payment obligations into the general cap, basket and 18-month window unless we remember to carve each one out. Reject the default. The clause should operate the other way: limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated. |
| **Fundamental/Title (Seller "administrative simplicity")** | Same cap and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% of price, minimum 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Non-negotiable. A title failure on a AUD 24m share purchase capped at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month window is unacceptable. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Require a Fundamental Warranty schedule (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, solvency) with its own regime. |
| **Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct** | Not mentioned at all – and cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 purport to apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" | Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable. **No one on our side may waive this.** | The silence is the problem: read with the "all Claims of any nature" language and the "all limitations apply to all Claims" default, the draft would attempt to cap and time-bar fraud. Insert an express, non-derogable fraud carve-out across cl 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5. This is not a trading chip. |
| **Exclusive remedy / non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)** | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Must not catch fraud, title/capacity, specific indemnities or statutory claims (e.g. Australian Consumer Law misleading-conduct claims cannot be contracted out of in any event) | Narrow to General Warranty Claims; express carve-outs for fraud, Fundamental Warranties, specific indemnities, covenants and non-excludable statutory rights. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**Whole-data-room / public-register disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2).** The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, the accounts, statutory registers and anything publicly searchable. This is the opposite of our specific-fair-disclosure standard. The practical effect is that any matter buried in DD-002 to DD-012 – however poorly flagged – becomes disclosed against every warranty. Reject. The standard should be: disclosed only if fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. General data-room disclosure, public-register disclosure and "prudent search" deeming should all be deleted. Note DL 1.4 (no admission of anything) sits uneasily with a letter that purports to disclose everything – the Seller wants the benefit of disclosure without the burden of characterising any of it.

**Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3).** "No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." This is a blanket actual-and-constructive-knowledge bar, extended to advisers, and keyed to "discoverable" rather than known. Combined with the whole-data-room disclosure it would effectively eliminate warranty protection. Delete. If any knowledge concept survives, playbook permits only a seller-side qualifier: "so far as the Seller is aware" meaning the actual knowledge of named Seller individuals after reasonable enquiry – and never applicable to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### C. Conditions and completion mechanics

**Bluefen (cl 3/6.3).** Seller Update: "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2: no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. Playbook requires (i) effective consent *and* (ii) evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both *before* Completion, and treats reasonable endeavours as insufficient for a material customer. Push back on all three limbs: condition precedent = consent in agreed form plus evidence of condition satisfaction, no "satisfied on delivery" deeming, and an all-reasonable/best-endeavours standard with an information covenant. Consider a termination right and a price/retention mechanism if consent is conditional or not forthcoming.

**Riverlark (cl 2/7).** Seller proposes a post-Completion release of a ~AUD 3.2m facility. Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms it is unpaid and no discharge is in the room. Playbook: current payout letter, repayment direct from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval – neither exists. Require a payout letter (addressed to buyer, with per-diem) and deed of release/PPSR discharge delivered at Completion, funded from the price in the funds flow. Also check the DD-003 cl 8.1 change-of-control – a share sale may itself be an event of default absent bank consent.

**Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL para 5).** Seller says the AUD 420,000 DD-005 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. The Disclosure Letter confirms they are not in the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs. These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company that crystallise on our transaction – if not funded, the Company (i.e. we) pays them post-Completion. Require either a specific funds-flow line item (gross AUD 420,000 plus superannuation, payroll tax and any other triggered on-costs) deducted from the price or paid by Seller at Completion, or treatment as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free adjustment, with a specific indemnity. The "matter for the Seller" phrasing is not a commitment and must be converted into one.

### D. Specific risk items

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1).** Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate". DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on clearance of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room. The real exposure is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own the IP it is selling us. Broaden the indemnity to cover non-ownership, third-party claims, re-procurement and loss of use of SOW3 materials, while preserving the cure route (pay the balance, obtain confirmatory assignment pre-Completion). Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified in both directions: require a bank-verified payment history and, ideally, a pre-Completion cure as a condition. Keep this indemnity outside the general cap/basket/time regime.

**Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006).** Seller: "preliminary", "not expected to be material". The Disclosure Letter is more candid: ~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external address, with access, scope and notification status unknown. We must not accept a materiality conclusion the Seller's own letter says cannot yet be drawn. Equally, we should not assert a confirmed breach or demand a number. Require: log preservation covenant; completion of the investigation with findings delivered pre-Completion; ongoing updates; a specific indemnity (uncapped by the general regime) for losses arising from the incident including any regulatory/notification costs; and a bring-down disclosure. Decide after findings whether price, retention or walk right is engaged.

**Sandbar renewals (DD-008/011).** Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter: three related AUD 110,000 renewals, deliberately to be read together, with no statement on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Playbook: assess, no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Request the contracts and timing, confirm whether any amount is accrued but unpaid at Completion (which would fall into working capital/Debt under normal mechanics), and whether splitting into three AUD 110,000 tranches has any approval-threshold purpose. No price demand at this stage.

**Office lease (DD-007) / Mossvale (DD-009).** Not flagged as consents by the Seller and the Disclosure Letter is careful not to say consent is required. Verify the notification obligation on DD-007 is complied with pre-Completion; review DD-009 ourselves for change-of-control language rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation.

### E. Tax, IP and title

**Tax / IP "settled under the general regime".** Not settled. Playbook treats Tax and IP as OPEN and separate categories. Under the Seller's draft they would be capped at AUD 4.8m, subject to a AUD 250k deductible and time-barred at 18 months – wholly inappropriate for tax (limitation periods run from assessment, not Completion) and for IP in a software/analytics business. Respond that these remain open and will be addressed in a separate Tax Indemnity and IP warranty/indemnity package. Do not assume unlimited liability; do not accept the general regime.

**Title "evidenced by DD-012".** The Disclosure Letter itself (para 10) concedes DD-012 is merely the source the Seller relies on. A company-maintained register is an internal document, not independent proof. Require: ASIC company extract and historical search; PPSR search against Company and Seller; certified copies of share certificates, transfer forms and board approvals; Seller constitutional authority and board resolution; absence-of-encumbrance confirmation; and a Fundamental Warranty on title under the separate regime above.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright (not tradable):**
1. Fundamental/Title warranties in the general regime – require separate regime, 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
2. Absence of a fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out – insert across all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance; no one on our side can waive this.
3. Cl 8.3 blanket buyer-knowledge bar (including advisers and "discoverable" matters) – delete.
4. Whole-data-room / public-register / prudent-search deemed disclosure – replace with specific fair disclosure.
5. "All limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise" and "all Claims of any nature" language – reverse the default; keep Title/Tax/IP/indemnity/covenant/payment categories separate.
6. Tax/IP "settled" – record as OPEN, separate regime.

**Counter at playbook starting positions (fallbacks require Amelia Frost written authority, none given):**
7. Cap: 25% / AUD 6.0m (Seller has pitched our 20% fallback – do not accept without authority).
8. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, tipping (first-dollar).
9. General claims period 24 months.

**Completion mechanics – convert Seller statements into binding deliverables:**
10. Bluefen: CP = effective consent in agreed form + evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied, pre-Completion; no "satisfied on delivery"; stronger endeavours standard.
11. Riverlark: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion; post-Completion release only with irrevocable bank undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
12. DD-005 bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus super/payroll tax/on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded/Debt, with indemnity.

**Specific risks:**
13. Ironquay: broaden indemnity to IP ownership/loss-of-use, preserve SOW3 cure, seek pre-Completion cure; verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
14. DD-006: log preservation, completed investigation and updates pre-Completion, specific indemnity; no materiality concession and no numeric demand either way.
15. Sandbar: information request and assessment only; no automatic Debt/price treatment.
16. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR/document evidence; DD-012 insufficient.

**Process:**
17. Require a refreshed Disclosure Letter and warranty bring-down at signing and Completion (current letter is dated 22 September 2026).
18. Seek Amelia Frost's instructions now on whether, and in what package, the 20% cap and 18-month fallbacks may be deployed, so we are not negotiating without authority.

Happy to prepare the mark-up of cl 8, 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5 and Schedule 7 and a draft response letter on these points.

### E. Tax, IP and title

**Tax / IP "settled under the general regime".** Not settled. Playbook treats Tax and IP as OPEN and separate categories.
